Author: Tinhampton
Co-author: Solringen (Haymarket)

Forum Thread: https://forum.nationstates.net/viewtopic.php?f=9&t=569108
Proposal: https://www.nationstates.net/page=UN_view_proposal/id=tinhampton_1755101235

Cast your vote by reacting to this message. You can also discuss below. Information here may be used to construct an IFV.

:tep_for:  = FOR / AYE
:tep_against:  = AGAINST / NAY
:tep_abstain:  = TEP ABSTAINS
:tep_present:  = NO OPINION / PRESENT

> Angered that GA#52 declares that where "a compelling governmental interest exists to protect the health and welfare of the people, the right of governments to seize food to supply to victims of such crises is granted, so long as such seizure is not detrimental to the larger population," effectively allowing states to steal food from private entities - such as businesses, charities, and middle-class individuals - without regards to any nutritional or other assistance they may have received from abroad, and in particular while demanding the pre-existence of such a "compelling government interest" as will almost inevitably arise during such crises,
Strongest argument. The rest are pretty flimsy

> Concerned that GA#52 merely requires the International Food Welfare Organization to distribute "food rations to the people of nations undergoing severe economic depression, famine, or conflict which causes a shortage of food" without also requiring them to be culturally sensitive, nutritious, or even free from outside poisons,
I hate that we lost the committee rule. Now we can opportunistically assume committees will incompetently poison people

> Baffled by the target resolution's insistence that a singular World Assembly Seedbank be created to store all manner of seeds "as volunteered by nations," even though the danger that would be posed by its destruction would be immeasurably massive,
Baffled by the existence of a headquarters for the WA, even though the danger that would be posed by its destruction… yeah not buying it
Changed the channel name: [NEXT] GA - Repeal "Food Welfare Act"
Registering myself as against. This is complete slop

> Concerned that GA#52 merely requires the International Food Welfare Organization to distribute "food rations to the people of nations undergoing severe economic depression, famine, or conflict which causes a shortage of food" without also requiring them to be culturally sensitive, nutritious, or even free from outside poisons,
Shamelessly exploiting the committee rule getting axed, don't you just love it? In what world does giving a WA body the authority to provide food mean that WA body is going to lace the food with poison? The organization isn't even required to distribute those surpluses in a particular way. The authors could've convincingly argued that establishing a vague surplus donation system with no elaboration is problematic. Instead, they went for this drivel.
> Angered that GA#52 declares that where "a compelling governmental interest exists to protect the health and welfare of the people, the right of governments to seize food to supply to victims of such crises is granted, so long as such seizure is not detrimental to the larger population," effectively allowing states to steal food from private entities - such as businesses, charities, and middle-class individuals - without regards to any nutritional or other assistance they may have received from abroad, and in particular while demanding the pre-existence of such a "compelling government interest" as will almost inevitably arise during such crises,
Stealing food from vulnerable people during a crisis would both fail to satisfy the compelling interest and be detrimental to the population. And if they've received sufficient nutritional and other assistance from abroad then there's no crisis anymore, is there? The "middle-class individuals" part is a nice touch 🙄

> Baffled by the target resolution's insistence that a singular World Assembly Seedbank be created to store all manner of seeds "as volunteered by nations," even though the danger that would be posed by its destruction would be immeasurably massive,
This is completely ridiculous. It's so ridiculous that even the WAHQ repeal didn't go for that kind of argument when repealing the establishment of *a singular physical headquarters for the entire WA*. Are we going to repeal the library compact for being vulnerable to arson and every resolution that makes a database for being vulnerable to cyberattacks?

> Convinced that aspiring to eliminate "protectionist practices... [with] the potential to severely harm international food trade" should not be a WA priority, given that protectionism helps developing economies to avoid being undercut by developed, industrialised countries, especially in niche agricultural areas, and
That's the argument they went for? Seriously? They could've convincingly argued that "INITIATES the gradual reduction of protectionist and other practices" is meaningless nonsense. Instead, they're saying that tariffs are actually good while using weasel words to get around the fact that the clause empowers a committee to *review and regulate* particularly problematic protectionist practices (hey that's alliteration!).

> Concluding that GA#52's micromanagement in all spheres of famine management - from agriculture to stockpiling to distribution - is massively detrimental to the people of all nations...
Boilerplate lazy appeal to natsov
Crap repeal

> New simplified ruleset: As detailed below, with the headline changes including the removal of the rules against duplication, contradiction, and on veracity of repeals.
Basically you’ll be able to pass resolutions that do the same thing other resolutions already do, contradict other resolutions, and lie in repeals
This stems from the fact that NS moderators - almost none of whom have GA experience - are currently judging GA proposal legality

The GA, being an international law roleplay, is naturally really technical and goes into arcane topics. We had a body called the General Secretariat (GenSec) doing legality rulings for about a decade, until a few months ago. They were a semi-autonomous group of experienced GA players. But then a big scandal happened where they resigned in protest after the site director threatened one of them for asking for bereavement leave after his daughter died, which the site admins used to get rid of the body permanently

GenSec was formed in the first place because moderators without GA experience could not keep up with GA legality questions. Instead of reconstituting gensec, their new approach is to gut the rules to make it easier for them to interpret them without experience
Mind you, GenSec became kind of a clown show in its last days. But this was just about the worst way of addressing anything
